Regular Council Meeting
CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
ACTION AGENDA
The Action Agenda of the City Council Meeting is a document provided immediately following the Council Meeting in order for staff and the public to be aware of the business transacted and actions taken by Council. This is a preliminary draft and not a public record. The meeting's legal record is the Minutes approved by the City Council.
SOLANA BEACH CITY COUNCIL
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY and PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
Joint REGULAR Meeting
WEDNESDAY, MAY 12, 2010
6:19 P.M.
CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS
635 S.HIGHWAY 101
SOLANA BEACH, CALIFORNIA
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
NOTICE
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, persons with a disability may request an agenda in appropriate alternative formats as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should direct such request to the City Clerk's office at (858) 720-2400 or by email at least 72 hours before the meeting.
As a courtesy to all meeting attendees, please set cellular phones and pagers to silent mode and engage in conversations outside the Council Chambers.
The Regular Meetings of the City Council are scheduled for the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays and are broadcast live on Cox Communications, Channel 19, and Time Warner, Channel 24. Council meetings are archived and available for viewing. The video taping of meetings are maintained as a permanent record and contain a detailed account of the proceedings.
A full City Council agenda packet with backup information is available at City Hall, at the Solana Beach branch of the San Diego County Library (157 Stevens Ave.), and online www.ci.solana-beach.ca.us at least 72 hours prior to the meeting. Agenda related writings or documents regarding an agenda item and that are received after the distribution of the agenda but at least 1 hour 30 minutes prior to the meeting will be available for public viewing at City Hall and posted online with the agenda.

Solana Beach City Council, Redevelopment Agency, and Public Financing Authority

JOINT REGULAR MEETING
Wednesday, May 12, 2010
06:19 P.M.
City Hall Council Chambers, 635 S. Highway 101, Solana Beach, California
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL:
Present:
Campbell, Heebner, Kellejian, Roberts, and Nichols.
Absent:
None.
Also Present:
David Ott, City Manager
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney
Angela Ivey, City Clerk
Dennis Coleman, Finance Director
Wende Protzman, Dir. Admin. Serv/Deputy City Mgr
Tina Christiansen, Community Dev. Dir.
Mo Sammak, City Engineer/Public Works Dir.
Mayor Campbell called the meeting to order at 6:19 pm.
FLAG SALUTE:
Mr. Boyd led the flag salute.
APPROVAL OF AGENDA:
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Heebner.
Motion carried unanimously.

1.
Bike to work day
Mayor Campbell presented a proclamation for Bike to Work Day.

(Ceremonial items that do not contain in-depth discussion and no action/direction.)

This portion of the agenda provides an opportunity for members of the public to address the City Council on items relating to City business and not appearing on today’s agenda by submitting a speaker slip (located on the back table) to the City Clerk. Council may refer items to the City Manager for placement on a future agenda. The maximum time allotted for each presentation is THREE MINUTES (SBMC 2.04.190). Please be aware of the timer light on the Council Dais.
Roger Boyd stated that he had been a resident of the City for 25 years, that he had formed a Safety Committee called, "Safer Solana Beach Citizens Committee" to address safety concerns on the I-5/Lomas Santa Fe interchange, that Council then created an Ad-Hoc Committee to review various safety issues, that the implemented actions included a raised median on the west bound lane of Lomas Santa Fe to separate the bike lane and motor vehicle lanes, removal of the 55 mile signs from the north and sound bound exit ramps, and restriping the lanes on Lomas Santa Fe. under the bridge from double yellow to double, double yellow to prevent vehicles from turning left onto the I-5 norhtbound ramp. He stated that the Committee’s work was completed and thanked the City for their assistance on the safety concerns.
Councilmember Heebner thanked the group for their work and stated that the artwork on the I-5 walls would be paid by Caltrans.
Marilee McLean stated that she was happy to see commercial recycling on the agenda, that she wanted to publically acknowledge American Assetts for their progress on providing commercial recycling dumps behind all their buildings, and she thanked them for their steps towards sustainability.
COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENTS:
Council reported community announcements.

A.
CONSENT CALENDAR: (Action Items) (Items A.1. - A.4.)
Items listed on the Consent Calendar are to be acted in a single action of the City Council unless pulled for discussion.
Any member of the public may address the City Council on an item of concern by submitting to the City Clerk a speaker slip
(located on the back table) before the Consent Calendar is addressed.
Those items removed from the Consent Calendar by a member of the Council will be trailed to the end of the agenda,
while Consent Calendar items removed by the public will be discussed immediately after approval of
the Consent Calendar.
A.1.
Waive the reading of Ordinances.
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Approve waiving the text reading of ordinances on this agenda pursuant to Solana Beach Municipal Code Section 2.04.460.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Nichols.
Motion carried unanimously.

Register of Demands. (File 0300-30)

Ratify the list of demands for April 3, 2010 through April 16, 2010.

Motion carried unanimously.

Re-Establishing the La Colonia Park Ad Hoc. (File 0410-48)

1.
Adopt Resolution 2010-050 re-establishing the La Colonia Park Ad Hoc Committee until May 11, 2011; and
2.
Re-appoint the current Councilmembers serving on the committee, Deputy Mayor Heebner and Councilmember Nichols OR appoint new members.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Nichols to re-appoint existing members.
Motion carried unanimously.

Asphalt and Concrete Repair Project Fiscal Year 2009/10, Bid No. 2009-08. (File 0400-10)

1.
Adopt Resolution 2010-049:
a.
Authorizing the City Council to accept as complete the 2009/10 Asphalt and Concrete Repair Project, Bid No. 2009-08, constructed by PAL General Engineering, Inc.
b.
Approving the final cost of the project at $195,620.68.
c.
Authorizing the City Clerk to file a Notice of Completion.

Motion carried unanimously.
NOTE: The City Council shall not begin a new agenda item after 10:30 p.m. unless approved by a unanimous vote of all members present. (SBMC 2.04.070)

PUBLIC HEARINGS: (Items B.1 - B.2.)
This portion of the agenda provides citizens an opportunity to express their views on a specific issue as required by law
after proper noticing by submitting a speaker slip (located on the back table) to the City Clerk .
After considering all of the evidence, including written materials and oral testimony,
the City Council must make a decision supported by findings and the findings must be supported by substantial evidence in the record.
An applicant or designees for a private development/business project, for which the public hearing is being held,
is allotted a total of fifteen minutes to speak, as per SBMC 2.04.210. A portion of the fifteen minutes may be saved to respond to those who speak in opposition.
All other speakers have three minutes each. Please be aware of the timer light on the Council Dais.
B.1.
Five Year Regional Transportation Improvement Program (RTIP) for Fiscal Years 2011 through 2015. (File 0150-55)

1.
Report Council disclosures
2.
Public Hearing: Open the public hearing, receive public testimony, close the public hearing.
3.
Adopt Resolution 2010-048 approving the TransNet Local Street Improvement Program list of projects for Fiscal Years 2011 through 2015.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item.
Mo Sammak, City Engineer, presented a powerpoint reviewing the 2011 - 2015 Regional Transportation Improvement Program (RTIP). He stated that the City had two projects that fell within the RTIP which included the Highway 101 Revitalization project and the Marine View Improvement project.
Council and Staff discussed the status of the Marine View Improvement project
Mayor Campbell opened the public hearing.
MOTION: Moved by Kellejian and seconded by Heebner to close the public hearing.
Motion carried unanimously.
MOTION: Moved by Kellejian and seconded by Heebner.
Motion carried unanimously.
B.2.
Development Review Permit (DRP) for 336 N. Granados Ave., Applicant: Hans and Jennifer Richter, Case No. 17-10-03 (File 0600-40)
The proposed project meets the minimum objective requirements under the SBMC, is consistent with the General Plan and may be found, as conditioned, to meet the discretionary findings required as discussed in this report to approve a DRP.
Therefore, Staff recommends that the City Council:
1.
Report Council disclosures;
2.
Conduct the Public hearing: Open the Public Hearing, Receive Public Testimony, Close the Public Hearing;
3.
Find the project exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to Section 15332 of the State CEQA Guidelines; and
4.
If the City Council makes the requisite finds and approves the project, adopt Resolution 2010-047 conditionally approving a Development Review Permit, for a new two-story, single-family residence of 3,676 square feet including the garage and detached structure at 336 N. Granados Avenue.
Councilmember Nichols recused himself from the item .
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item requesting a Development Review Permit and stated now coming back with different project.
Corey Johnson, presented a powerpoint.
Council and Staff discussion ensued regarding the entire lot coming down 3 ft. and that the property next door could also request the lowering of their building in the future, that plans had been reviewed and verified that drainage would work if constructed properly, and that the project would not qualify for the Scoop program.
Mayor Campbell asked the applicant if he wanted to speak and he said he was available for questions.
Council disclosed their familiarity with the project.
Mayor Campbell opened the public hearing.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Heebner to close the public hearing.
Motion carried 4/0/1
(Recuse:
Nichols.)
MOTION: Moved by Heebner and seconded by Roberts.
Motion carried 4/0/1
(Recuse:
Nichols.)
C.
STAFF REPORTS: (Items C.1. - C.5)
Submit speaker slips to the City Clerk.
Submit speaker slips to the City Clerk
C.1.
Support of AB 32, the Global Warming Solutions Act of 2006 (File 0480-70)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Adopt Resolution 2010-051 supporting the continued implementation of AB 32.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item.
Dan King, Management Analyst, presented a powerpoint stating that the requirement was a mandatory reduction of greenhouse gases by the year 2020.
Council and Staff discussion ensued regarding the fact that there was no fiscal impact to adhere to adopt all requirement, that there may be costs in the future for other stages of compliance, to consider delaying implementation, and that there was no reason that it could not be adhered to now.
Lane Sharman (time donated by Mr. Hetz) thanked Council for addressing the issue, that there was a greater cost of inaction than action for subsequent generations, that action today was a step in the right direction, that there were a lot of negatives about Assembly Bill 32 which were legitimate concerns but were not reasons to bury the head in the sand, and that he thought that many in the public would come to volunteer.
Roger Boyd said that he lived in the City and asked Council to support AB32, that $1 million had been raised to delay the initiative, that this would be expeditious action and was supported by City staff, and that it would be an important signal to the region that the City was green.
Don Christiansen says he was AB32 was a result of a meeting in 2006 and signed by Schwarzeneger, that he was surprised it was being threatened, that what happened in the state often led the way to the rest of the states and the world, thanked the City for showing a strong leadership position, that a business group in northern California that commissioned a study by consultants to study the results of implementing AB32 and the report stating that it would cost tens of thousands of dollars to residents to implement, and that since then Universities have discredited this report.
Siobhon Foley said that she was the Director for Education and Outreach at the California for Education on Sustainable Energy, a non-profit, that she applauded the resolution to support AB32, that the challenges faced are devestating is left unchecked, that the model did not address the cost of doing nothing, that it was importannt for local and state govenrment to step up, that clean energy jobs were on the rise even during a down economy, and that the implementation of AB32 would cause residents to make wise energy choices.
Aaron Contorer presented a powerpoint. He said he was the Chairman of Equionox Center which provided research and was was non-partisan. He said that AB32 tried to accomplish 3 things including reducing danger to qualify of life, reducing potential economic damage, and creating massive hi-tech employment and business growth. He reviewed graphs
Steve Goetsch reported findings from the United Nations including the threat to the amazon forest, coral, amphibious species, and that it was a time when could not be put off any longer. He said that
Bruce Bekkar said he was representing the Energy Issues Advisory Committee and was a resident of Del Mar. He said that they supported the resolution, that he had represented his City at ECLEI, that the oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico showed the risks of continuing to do business as usual, that this was under attack by some state officials as well as some elected candidates, and that they were planning on bring it to their City Council.
Alissa Barrow said that she was an environmental engineering student and UCSD, that she would be entering the job market and was especially concerned about AB32, that if AB32 is rolled back it would kill the green economy in California, that this was the first legislation of its kind, that the rest of the world has been talking but no action had been taken yet, and that California was a roll model to the country and the world.
Eric Lodge, said he lived on Marview Lane, that the pitch was made that if the voters did not pass that jobs would be lost, that during this tough economy that green objectives have been achieved as well as an uptake in the green economy, and that the loss of jobs was a bogus claim.
Council thanked Staff for the work and efforts, consider adding a clause to not support the current ongoing initiative to stop it, that it may already be understood, and that it stated to suspend the initiative or delay it and did not say to kill it so may want to adjust it.
MOTION: Moved by Heebner and seconded by Roberts to approve with modifications.
Motion carried unanimously.
Mayor Campbell recessed the meeting for a break at 7:40 p.m. and reconvened at 7:46 p.m.
